reason: The finding's own crux measurement is wrong, and the code comment it tries to overturn is correct. Driven at 1440x960 and 1280x900 in owner-editing: .b-stick does compute position: sticky (top: 40px), but the rail is NOT stuck at the default scroll. Measured .b-stick rect top by scrollY: 0->231, 100->131, 191->40 (sticks), 900->40, 1170->-136 (unsticks against .b-two's bottom). So the first .b-step travels 829 -> 638 -> 522 as the page scrolls 0 -> 600 -> 1200. The finding states 'I watched the first .b-step hold while the page scrolled from 0 to 1200'; it moved 307px. The steppers move 1:1 with the page for the first 191px of scroll and again past ~1035. 191px is 4.8x the 40px height of the control being repeatedly pressed. The proposed fix's very first scroll, from the default scrollY 0 after the second press, is scrollBy(~521) - which spends all 191px of that drift. I mapped the control geometry and then re-ran elementFromPoint at each stepper's own centre after scrolling to 191: the point that was 'Move a week earlier' (x 203-247, y 829-869) is then occupied by 'Done' (x 203-264, y 1034-1073). 'Delete this moment' (y 1098-1137) sits 64px below that, inside the further ~135px of drift available at the document's tail. So the fix as proposed puts a destructive/dismissive control under a point the owner is repeat-pressing - precisely the failure the comment gates against - which is worse than the complaint. The second half of the finding is not reachable at all. There is exactly one [data-act=add] control in owner-flight and it sits at document y~107, above the list, on screen only while scrollY < ~146; at scrollY 900 it is at top -793. I reproduced the finding's 'new row at top -456' only by calling .click() from script on a control 993px above the viewport. Through a real pointer or keyboard focus the browser brings the control into view first, and at every reachable scroll the created row (document y~444) and its title field are both on screen. What survives is only that at >=1280 the edited row's .b-copy runs from 696 to 1704 over eight presses while scrollY stays 0 - true, but at desk width the rail carries permanent feedback that is on screen throughout (the mono readout, measured reading 'Saturday 29 August 2026 - in 44 days', plus the ceiling note), the first press keeps the row on screen, and the ladder is a scrolling document there by design. Trading that for a stepper that walks 191px out from under the hand and seats 'Done' where it was is not an improvement at a 9.5 bar.
